purpose: Tazarotene is used to treat acne, psoriasis, and to help improve the look of fine wrinkles, dark spots, and rough skin. It helps clear up skin by speeding up the natural turnover of skin cells. Your doctor may prescribe it for one or more of these conditions depending on your needs.
how_it_works: Tazarotene works by attaching to special receptors in your skin cells that control how they grow and shed. It speeds up the process of old, damaged, or abnormal skin cells being replaced by newer, healthier ones. Think of it like hitting a reset button on your skin to help it look and act more normally.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are skin irritation, redness, peeling, dryness, and a burning or stinging feeling where you apply it. These effects are usually mild and often get better after the first few weeks as your skin adjusts to the medication.
warnings: Do NOT use tazarotene if you are pregnant or trying to get pregnant, as it can cause serious harm to an unborn baby — use reliable birth control while using it. Avoid getting it in your eyes, mouth, or nose. Your skin will be more sensitive to sunlight, so always wear sunscreen and protective clothing outdoors. Do not use on skin that is sunburned, windburned, or broken.
typical_dosing: For most adults, a thin layer is applied once daily in the evening to clean, dry skin in the affected area. Use only a pea-sized amount — a little goes a long way. Always follow your doctor or pharmacist's specific instructions, as the strength and how often you apply it may vary based on your condition.
